summary: Decoded all 6 calls to the ui_window_create thunk (file offset 0xbbb6) in wpcmk.ovr. Three calls are in the top-level wpcmk entry function (FUN_59e0, called from wbase) and create PERSISTENT windows used by all 17 screens. Two calls are in ui_train_attribute_picker_grid (0x229c, screen-14). One call is in ui_welcome_animation (0x1ae9, screen-13). Screens 00-12, 15, 16 exclusively reuse the 3 persistent windows; screen-13 adds 1 overlay window; screen-14 adds 2 overlay windows. The task description's claim that 'creation_ui_init is at 0x0d13' is correct — 0x0d13 is a real function called from master at 0x4e6c — but 0x0d13 does NOT create windows; it only initializes UI content within the already-existing persistent windows. The actual window creation happens in FUN_59e0 before the master is ever called.
method: Exhaustive search for E8 (near-call) bytes whose relative offset resolves to target 0xbbb6 via `(file_offset + 3 + signed_rel16) & 0xffff == 0xbbb6`. Found exactly 6 call sites. For each site, traced the 8 push instructions immediately before the call using raw byte inspection. Call argument order: right-to-left push means last pushed = x_byte ([bp+0x04]), first pushed = arg8 ([bp+0x12]). Also checked which window handles ([0x546e], [0x56ca], [0x56cc]) are referenced in key screen driver functions via pattern matching for push-word-ptr-XXXX byte sequences.

persistent_windows_creating_function.name: FUN_59e0 (unnamed in naming pass; top-level wpcmk entry called from wbase)
persistent_windows_creating_function.note: This function creates all 3 persistent windows, then calls ui_setup_creation_windows (0x5093), then shows the roster management menu. It is NOT called from within wpcmk.ovr itself. The only apparent call from within the overlay file is a false positive: the byte 0xE8 at file offset 0x000e is the HIGH BYTE of a 'push word 0xE8A1' operand in the 16-byte overlay header, not an executed CALL opcode.

findings.claim: Name entry uses [0x56ca] (the bottom status bar window) for the text input prompt. wpcmk_create_via_empty_slot (0x50f2) first calls ui_setup_creation_windows(0x546e, 0x56ca), displays msg 0x44c in [0x56ca], reads window metadata from [0x56ca]+6/+7 for cursor position, then calls ui_text_input_editor with [0x56ca] as the window arg. No new windows are created.

evidence.details: 50F8: FF 36 CA 56 = push word [0x56ca]; 50FC: FF 36 6E 54 = push word [0x546e]; 5100: E8 90 FF = call 0x5093 (ui_setup_creation_windows). Then 511A: FF 36 CA 56 = push [0x56ca] for 0xbda7. Then 5179: FF 36 CA 56 = push [0x56ca] for call to 0xf0 (ui_text_input_editor). No E8 xx xx resolving to 0xbbb6 anywhere in 0x50f2..0x51c6.

findings.claim: Spell school animation (ui_welcome_animation, 0x1ae9) creates ONE new temporary window for the animation overlay. Call at file offset 0x1b28: x=20, y=4, w=20, h=16, attr=0x19, border=0xffff (plain). Handle stored at [bp-0x4] (local stack var). This window sits in the right half of the main creation area (x=20..40, y=4..20 = pixels 160..320, 32..160). The persistent window [0x56ca] is passed as an arg to ui_welcome_animation but window creation happens inside. After the animation completes, the temporary window is discarded (not stored in a DGROUP handle).

evidence.details: Push sequence before call at 0x1b28 (read last-push-first = x_byte): 1B0B: mov ax,0x0; 1B0F/1B0F: push ax TWICE = arg8=0, arg7=0. 1B10: mov ax,0xffff; 1B13: push = border_style=0xffff. 1B14: mov ax,0x19; 1B17: push = attribute=0x19. 1B18: mov ax,0x10; 1B1B: push = h_cells=16. 1B1C: mov ax,0x14; 1B1F: push = w_cells=20. 1B20: mov ax,0x4; 1B23: push = y_byte=4. 1B24: mov ax,0x14; 1B27: push = x_byte=20. Return value: 1B2E: mov [bp-0x4], ax. Used by creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step(0x15d7) and ui_class_menu_with_qualification(0x1158).

findings.claim: Skill training (ui_train_attribute_picker_grid, 0x229c) creates TWO new temporary windows per call. Window 1 (call at 0x22bf): x=20, y=4, w=20, h=16, attr=0x16, plain. Window 2 (call at 0x22e5): x=21, y=7, w=19, h=8, attr=0x17, plain. The outer window (call at 0x22bf) occupies the same pixel area (160x128) as the spell-school animation window from screen-13. The inner sub-window (call at 0x22e5) overlaps with [0x56cc] but is taller by 5 cells. wpcmk_train_skill_pillar (0x28d4) calls ui_train_attribute_picker_grid; the function runs up to 4 times (one per pillar). Both handles stored in stack locals [bp-0x2] and [bp-0x4] and discarded after the function returns.

evidence.details: Call at 0x22bf — pushes from 0x22a2: 22A5+22A6: push 0x0 TWICE (arg8=0, arg7=0); 22A7: push 0xffff (border_style); 22AB: push 0x16 (attr); 22AF: push 0x10 = 16 (h_cells); 22B3: push 0x14 = 20 (w_cells); 22B7: push 0x4 (y_byte); 22BB: push 0x14 = 20 (x_byte). Return -> [bp-0x2]. Call at 0x22e5 — pushes from 0x22c8: 22CB+22CC: push 0x0 TWICE; 22CD: push 0xffff; 22D1: push 0x17 (attr); 22D5: push 0x8 = 8 (h_cells); 22D9: push 0x13 = 19 (w_cells); 22DD: push 0x7 (y_byte); 22E1: push 0x15 = 21 (x_byte). Return -> [bp-0x4]. After both creates: calls 0xed5a (clear [bp-4]), 0x1cb2 ([bp-2]), 0x1c37 ([bp-4]), then 0xe5b5 for [bp+6] (caller's arg). 6-cell grid loop at 0x2328 computes positions using [bp-0x4a] / [bp-0x4c] relative to window metadata.

findings.claim: Confirmation menu (inline in wpcmk_create_character_master at ~0x4f20). Uses [0x56ca] and [0x56cc] inferred from the screen-flow: calls func_0x0000ed5a (clear), func_0x0000e5b5 (refresh), func_0x0000bda7 (cursor), func_0x0000c2db (print msg 0x44f) — these same call patterns are used with [0x56ca] in all other menu screens; then ui_menu_picker_vertical uses [0x56cc] per the Task 2 decompile text: 'ui_menu_picker_vertical(*(int *)0x56ca, ..., 0x45a, ...)'. Note: The Task 2 finding cites '*(int *)0x56ca' not '*(int *)0x56cc' for the menu — this MAY indicate the confirm menu uses [0x56ca] directly for both label and picker, differing from race/class/alignment which use both. Confidence lowered to medium due to this ambiguity. No new windows created.

evidence.details: From screen-flow.json Task 2 findings: 'func_0x0000c2db(0x44f, window)' and 'local_6 = ui_menu_picker_vertical(*(int *)0x56ca, ..., 0x45a, ...)'. The first arg to ui_menu_picker_vertical is the window handle; here it is '*(int *)0x56ca' = the CONTENTS of address 0x56ca = [0x56ca] window handle. This is consistent with [0x56ca] being used as the picker window. Disasm verification of 0x4f20..0x4fae was not performed in this pass due to tooling constraint (ndisasm would confirm).

findings.claim: Roster save (roster_io_one_record + roster_save_all inline in master at ~0x4fae) is non-interactive disk I/O. No window interaction — no push-word-[window] references in the save code path. No new windows created.

evidence.details: From master window-ref scan of 0x4e47..0x5010: refs at 0x4ee5, 0x4efd, 0x4f01, 0x4f24, 0x4f2e, 0x4f4d, 0x4f5b — all at addresses BEFORE the 0x4f20 confirm menu region. After 0x4f5b there are no more window refs in the master. The save code starting ~0x4fae calls roster_io_one_record (0x1b), f0dc thunk, c772, f924, fdbd, fd76, fda5 — these are I/O primitives with no window args.

findings.note: No window updates during save. The screen display remains whatever was last shown by the confirmation menu.

persistent_windows.summary: Three windows created in FUN_59e0 (the top-level wpcmk entry function called from wbase) persist for the entire wpcmk session. All 17 screens reuse at least one of these.

windows.role: main creation area / character stat display

windows.typical_usage: Screen headers, msg labels, text input, personality animation, confirm menu

windows.role: right-side menu panel (19 cells wide, 13 rows tall)

open_questions: attribute interpretation: The attr field values (0x13, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x19) are raw bytes. In text-mode these would be (bg_nibble << 4 | fg_nibble) with EGA palette indices. In EGA graphics mode D (320x200), the interpretation may differ — likely still a packed color pair. Not cross-validated against live palette data in this pass.

screen-15-confirm window usage: The task 2 decompile text says 'ui_menu_picker_vertical(*(int *)0x56ca, ...)' which would make [0x56ca] (the bottom bar) the picker window — but this is a 5-row bottom bar, not the 13-row [0x56cc]. Possible interpretation: the confirm screen uses the bottom bar for both the prompt label AND the 2-choice menu, which would fit a 2-entry list inside 5 rows. Recommend verifying by disassembling 0x4f20..0x4fae.

FUN_59e0 formal name: This function is not in the naming pass (docs/re/findings/wpcmk-naming-pass.json). Suggested name: 'wpcmk_session_init_and_roster_ui'. It is the true top-level entry for wpcmk, called from wbase, and creates the 3 persistent windows before entering the roster management loop.

Does FUN_59e0 receive the window handles as args or return them to wbase? The function stores window handles in DGROUP at [0x546e], [0x56ca], [0x56cc] — so no arg passing is needed. The window handles live in the shared wroot DGROUP and are accessible to all overlays via the same DS.

Temporary windows in screen-13 and screen-14 are not stored in DGROUP — they live only in stack locals and are destroyed when the function returns. Confirm that the game engine actually destroys/frees these windows, or if they leak into the heap free list.

screen-14 inner window attr=0x17 vs [0x56cc] attr=0x15: The skill training grid sub-panel (0x17) has a slightly different attribute than the persistent right panel (0x15). These may appear in different colors if the attribute byte drives display properties.

Cell-to-pixel factor: The analysis assumes 8px per cell throughout (EGA mode D, 320x200 with 40-column text). The wroot-ui-window-struct.json confirms 'x_byte = top-left column in 8-pixel cells' and 'y_byte = top-left row in 8-pixel cells'. This should be cross-validated against a live DOSBox-X screenshot for one of the known windows.
